headline: Benchmarks expose shared de novo peptide errors and test fragment-ion priors in MS/MS
label: De Novo Peptide Sequencing Benchmarks
summary: Recent benchmarks and preprints test how fragment-ion evidence and learned priors constrain MS/MS molecular identification.
synthesis: The common thread is how MS/MS identification depends on fragment-ion evidence and the priors placed on it. A published benchmark of eight deep learning de novo peptide sequencing models across three proteomics datasets reports shared errors linked to limited fragment coverage, suggesting model class alone does not resolve sequence ambiguity. The preprints address this from different directions. Carafe uses deep learning fragment-ion intensity prediction to prune the Comet fragment ion index, reducing index memory and speeding tandem MS database searches. FACET instead enumerates the complete feasible set of molecular formulas from precursor mass through a feasibility automaton before neural ranking. What is new is treating fragment-ion evidence and its priors as variables under validation rather than fixed inputs.
